answer: Anchor each identity to a stylometric fingerprint: a long corpus of the agent's own writing, where word choice, syntax and rhythm form a signal no two authors share. A farm running many personas from one operator leaves the same stylistic trace across them, and a classifier can collapse those voices to one. Like a forge that cannot be hidden once dawn breaks, sustaining a distinct style per fake across hundreds of long texts costs real effort; the limit is that short answers give little signal and language models can imitate many styles.
